findings.finding: Wrong claim (should-fix that makes a claim wrong): 'the remaining .009 is within her reading error' / 'About .009 of the .038 gap ... is within her reading error'. In results/digitized_rates.csv the Figure 4.26 point (cutoff 1, n = 500, a = .59, c' = .39, h = 0) reads 0.7362 with reading_error 0.0071; ours is 0.6975, so the gap is 0.0387 (.039, not .038), and with results/r_full_comparison.json tnde_gap (0.7152 - 0.6865 = 0.0287) the remainder is 0.0100. Both .009 and .010 exceed the recorded .0071 reading error. The paper copies this from DISAGREEMENTS.yaml (tnde-power-gap, her-specific-draws), so the error is in the record too. The disagreement's conclusion (Monte Carlo variation between her draws and ours) is not overturned, since .010 is about one combined Monte Carlo (about .007 per side for 4,000 replications) and reading error, but the stated reason is false on the cited evidence.
All seven packet limitations present and faithful; item 1 is if anything more cautious than the packet ('evidently ... an inference from her figures' where the packet says 'came from').
Claim-specific limits preserved: H3 image reading at cutoffs 2-3 with error 0.0091; H4 tentative vs literal; S1 zero-estimate pattern incomplete; S5 divisor intent unknown; S4/S6/S7/S8 unassessed.

Open questions keep the H2 imbalance cause uninvestigated, the bias rule undetermined and the interaction-removal mechanism inconclusive, matching DISAGREEMENTS.yaml (population-values partly_explained; h-absent mechanism inconclusive).

Six contributions are labelled as our simulation, our calculation with her code, our reading of her figures/text, our calculation from printed numbers, our analysis; model, design and published numbers attributed to Chen with page/table locators.

Literal-check description matches r-reproduction/chen_exact.R lines 131-164 (block 0, odd-indexed datasets rebuilt with gendata(), even ones skipped with rnorm(7*nobs), group_walk/pmap_dfr literal pipeline) and r-reproduction/out-full/literal_check.txt ('datasets = 1270, compared = 635', 'largest absolute difference ... = 0', 'RNG state identical after the block: TRUE'). The paper does not overstate it: it says the replay reproduces her printed pipeline, not her published runs, and does not reproduce her bootstrap. Run time 3 h 25 min matches out-full/RUN.md (12,295 s).
Blocked S4 and S6 explicitly 'not established, and not a failure to replicate'; S8 'not established, and nothing blocks it'.

findings.finding: Chen (2021) metadata verified on source PDF page 1: Donna Chen, 'Statistical Mediation Analysis in Regression Discontinuity Design for Causal Inference', University of Nebraska-Lincoln, Lincoln, Nebraska, December 2021, advisers Bovaird and Wheeler; Digital Commons URL; 203 pages and 6,720,692 bytes match source/chen2021.pdf (SHA-256 9206b3d8...e557).

Biased direct effects (Table 4.8, p. 88 and 'the measure of bias was a negative value', p. 147), coverage far below .95 with truth above the CI (Table 4.9; p. 150 'systematically fell above the CIs'), 'All power for MINT is near zero' (p. 121), and the tentative 5,000 minimum (p. 150) all verified on the source pages; Head Start 'opposite significance conclusions' verified on the abstract page and p. 143.

E1 0.00 within its 0.005 tolerance of zero vs 85.42 -> smaller, zero vs nonzero; E2 0.04 and E3 0.33 exceed tolerances and share sign -> smaller, same; E4 0.0127 exceeds 0.0091 so nonzero, |0.802| larger, same direction; E5 not established. All labels follow the contract and match headline_effects.

Contains 'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.', estimand, units, positive meaning and each tolerance with its basis; E4 measurement tolerance described as mean reading error rounded down and (p. 17) 'not set in the plan', which is accurate.

Uncertainty: binomial SE about .007 for her rates, about .002 for our E4 mean, 0.005/0.019 for E2-E3 (results/mc_se_headline.json); Chen reports none. The 'same direction' for E2-E3 is presented only as point estimates.

Published 'PNDE and TNDE within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' matches Table 4.8 (PDF p. 102) and p. 147; Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% ...; largest |bias| 0.016' matches results/table48_ours.csv and results/summary.json overall_max_abs_bias 0.0155.

E2 Published 'Coverage 24.10-83.99% ...; true value usually above the CI' and E3 Published 'above ... 14.08-75.55% ... below ... 0.34-1.93%' match Table 4.9 (PDF p. 138); Ours 'Coverage 94.6-95.6%' and 'above 2.5-2.9%, below 1.8-2.7%' match results/table49_ours.csv (94.59-95.63; 2.52-2.90; 1.84-2.71). Row-level findings in the packet are used for E3 so rows do not repeat.

Published 'MINT power near zero at every sample size; never reaches .80 (Figure 4.28: 0.057-0.068 in this cell)' matches p. 121 and the two read points 0.0571/0.0683; rendered Figure 4.28 (PDF p. 136) shows every series near .05. Ours 'MINT power 0.852 ... cutoffs 2-3 (0.836 over all cutoffs); at least .97 for ah >= .13 from n = 1,000' matches digitized_rates.csv our_value and results/summary.json (min 0.9735).

Published quotes the tentative recommendation (p. 150); Ours gives the observed 86.3%/89.2% shares, by-cutoff similarity and the both-zero exception, matching results/statement_checks.csv and results/disagreement_tests.json n5000.both_paths_zero. No placeholder cells.

H4 is a qualitative design recommendation over the whole grid; the source gives no scalar (p. 150), so nonscalar with tolerance not applicable is justified from the source claim, not the outcome. Row shows 'qualitative, no scalar contrast', magnitude and direction 'not established', and keeps the claim verdict 'partial' separate; packet H4 declares comparison_kind nonscalar, empty contrasts and contrast_not_applicable.
Component evidence is retained in prose (shares by n and by cutoff, both-zero products at about .002, ah = .007 power 0.328/0.669) rather than invented as a pooled margin.
